raw_response:
I will still lean on what worked for me the last few years, because 9 mu is not big and every bag of fertilizer costs real money. Cotton is still my main crop, so I will give it the bigger share of land and inputs, because if cotton falls short the whole year feels tight. I do watch what people around me plant and use, and around Quzhou many people now use better seed for maize and cotton if the stand is more even and the yield is steadier. I will not cut fertilizer too hard at the start, because losing yield hurts more than spending a little extra. With well water in hand, I do not fear drought as much, so I can push cotton and maize a bit. Mungbean I will keep on a smaller piece, use less nitrogen, and mainly spend enough to get a clean stand and decent pods. For field work, I will mostly plough or rotary till before sowing, then topdress the heavier feeders after they get going.
